title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Iran sets two-day terms to reopen Hormuz
preheader: Trump says US still has one or two targets in Iran as Khamenei warns of response.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Sunday, November 01, 2026 — the 2 stories that matter most today, plus 3 updates on stories you're following and 4 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz can reopen in two days if US accepts conditions
stories.why_important: Iran's foreign minister said the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days. That would happen if Washington recognizes a new shipping route agreed with Oman and closes other routes. The strait is the world's most important oil bottleneck, and reopening it would ease energy markets and lower war risk.
stories.what_overlooked: The offer is conditional and has no public US response. Iran is also debating whether to keep its ban on nuclear weapons if fighting resumes.
stories.prediction: A US public response to Iran's conditions within 72 hours: acceptance would signal less tension; silence would leave Hormuz closed.

stories.story_title: Germany's Gen Z protests turn violent as rioters loot Frankfurt stores
stories.why_important: Tens of thousands marched in 34 German cities demanding better education and lower living costs. The daytime protests were largely peaceful, but hooded rioters looted stores in Frankfurt at night, part of a wave of youth-led unrest across Europe.
stories.what_overlooked: The looting overshadowed the demonstrations, and no nationwide arrest or injury count was immediately available.
stories.prediction: Police and organizers' next moves in Frankfurt within 72 hours; new clashes or a peaceful follow-up will show whether the movement stays mass.

quick_hits.text: London police arrested 139 people outside the US embassy for supporting Palestine Action, which Britain has banned as a terrorist group.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is open to a formal apology for Britain's slave trade but ruled out financial reparations.
Bolivia declared a state of emergency over El Nino, with drought affecting 78,000 families and killing more than 75,000 cattle.
Brazil's Lula da Silva won the presidential runoff with nearly 52% after trailing by 2.2 million votes in the first round.

The FBI blamed North Korea for the $6.3 billion Binance hack, and Binance said it will cover about 90% of customer losses.
